title: Private Deployments - VPC & On-Prem Reference Guide: Deployment, Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrades, and Customer Requirements
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:
This document is the canonical Redwood reference for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It consolidates deployment guides, supported reference architectures, on-prem packaging options, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade & rollback playbooks. Intended audience: platform engineers, SREs, solutions engineers, and customer infra teams performing or supporting Private deployments.

Key goals:
- Provide repeatable steps for initial deployment in customer VPCs and on-prem environments.
- Standardize packaging and installation artifacts (Docker/OCI images, Helm charts, install bundles).
- Define day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, scaling, incident procedures).
- Capture tested upgrade strategies and safe rollback procedures.
- Publish a customer requirements checklist to accelerate scoping and security reviews.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers Redwood Private control plane + serving runtime (inference nodes).
- Assumes customer network & security teams can provision required subnets, routes, and firewall rules.
- Does not cover custom model onboarding steps beyond model artifact placement and optional model registry integration (see related onboarding docs).

1) Quick Architecture Overview
- Control plane (managed by Redwood or customer, depending on deployment option) orchestrates config, telemetry, and auth.
- Serving plane runs as tenant-isolated clusters: Kubernetes (preferred) or air-gapped VM groups for legacy on-prem.
- Optional components: audit-logging forwarder, KMS/HSM connector, metrics exporter (Prometheus), and tracing collector (Jaeger).

Reference architectures (high level)
- Small (POC): 3 x inference nodes (GPU not required for tiny models), 2 x control replicas, single AZ, minimum observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana).
- Production (HA): 6+ inference nodes (GPUs), 3 control plane replicas across AZs, dedicated autoscaling group for serving, external KMS, centralized logging (ELK/CloudWatch), and a private registry for images.
- Regulated/air-gapped: install bundle (tarball), offline package registry, on-prem KMS/HSM, and strict egress restrictions.

Minimum hardware & software requirements (recommended)
| Component | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane | 3 vCPU, 8GB RAM | 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM | Small installs can co-host control components on dedicated nodes |
| Inference node (CPU) | 8 vCPU, 32GB RAM | 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM | For CPU models only |
| Inference node (GPU) | N/A | NVIDIA A10 / A100 or equivalent | GPU type depends on model performance profile |
| Kubernetes | 1.25+ | 1.26+ | Recommend managed K8s with CNI supporting IP routing |
| Storage | 100GB | 1TB | model artifacts and cache storage |

Networking requirements (VPC)
- Subnets: control plane subnet(s) + serving subnet(s) with route table entries.
- Security groups / firewalls: allow control plane <-> serving (TLS 443), metrics (TCP 9100/9090 internal), NTP, and outbound to KMS endpoints if external.
- NAT/GW: required for patching/downloads unless using offline registries.
- DNS: internal DNS entries for service discovery; TLS certs must be trusted by both sides.

2) On-prem Packaging and Installation Options
Supported packaging formats:
- Helm Charts (primary for Kubernetes installs)
- Operator + CRDs for advanced lifecycle automation
- Offline tarball with systemd units / containerd manifests for air-gapped installs

Installation patterns:
A) Kubernetes (recommended)
1. Prepare cluster: install metrics server, cert manager, and CNI.
2. Configure image registry (pull secrets or private registry mirror).
3. Apply RBAC and namespace policies.
4. helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood-inference.internal/helm
5. helm upgrade --install redwood-control redwood/redwood-control -f values-prod.yaml --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace
6. Apply serving node DaemonSet/Deployment: helm upgrade --install redwood-serving redwood/redwood-serving -f values-serving.yaml

B) Air-gapped / Offline
1. Provide offline bundle (sha256 sums included).
2. Customer mirrors images to their private registry and provides registry endpoint.
3. Apply manifests with local registry references.
4. Validate checksums and package signatures before starting services.

Packaging notes:
- Values files: values-prod.yaml must include resource requests/limits, nodeSelector (gpu=true), tolerations, and registry credentials.
- Artifacts are signed; the verifier checks signatures at install time.

3) Detailed VPC Deployment Guide (Step-by-step)
Pre-deployment checklist (customer):
- VPC CIDR blocks and subnet allocations for control and serving planes.
- KMS/HSM endpoint availability and IAM role with decrypt permissions.
- Private image registry credentials and network routes.
- VPN or Direct Connect for control plane if management is split.

Deployment steps:
1) Provision infra: create subnets, route tables, security groups.
2) Provision managed Kubernetes cluster or VM pool according to reference architecture.
3) Create registry secrets and upload values-prod.yaml to a secure S3 (or equivalent) location.
4) Install control plane (see Helm command above).
5) Install serving plane with GPU taints/nodes.
6) Post-install verification: health endpoints (/healthz), sample inference request, metrics ingestion.

Validation tests (automated):
- curl https://redwood-control.internal/healthz -> 200 OK
- kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -> all Running/Ready
- run load test at 10qps and validate latency 95th < 200ms for small models (adjust per profile)

4) Upgrade and Rollback Procedures
Principles:
- Always test upgrades in a staging environment that mirrors production.
- Prefer rolling upgrades with canary traffic to verify behavior.
- Keep previous image/version available for fast rollbacks.

Supported upgrade strategies:
- Canary rollouts: 5-10% traffic to new version for 30-60 minutes, then gradually increase.
- Blue/green: deploy new stack in parallel, flip traffic via load balancer / DNS.
- In-place rolling: sequential pod replacements with readiness gates (use when stateful changes are minimal).

Upgrade checklist:
1) Backup control plane DB and any metadata stores (take snapshot).
2) Create release notes and verify compatibility matrix for model-serving binary & config.
3) Promote canary image: helm upgrade --install --set image.tag=2029.11.1 redwood-control redwood/redwood-control -f values-canary.yaml
4) Monitor error rates, latency, and key metrics for 30-60 minutes.
5) If metrics are stable, advance rollout; otherwise rollback.

Rollback steps (fast rollback example for Helm):
1) helm rollback redwood-control 0 --namespace redwood-system
2) Verify pods return to previous version and health checks pass.
3) Restore DB snapshot if migration was applied and is incompatible.

Notes on DB migrations:
- Migrations must be reversible or guarded by feature flags.
- Apply migrations as a separate step with checkpoints and ability to pause.

5) Day-2 Operations (Runbook highlights)
Ownership and escalation:
- First responder: customer infra team / assigned Redwood SE during onboarding.
- Platform oncall: redwood-platform@redwood-inference.internal (escalate after 15 minutes).

Daily/weekly ops tasks:
- Verify backups completed and test restore monthly.
- Check queue depth and KV cache hit rates.
- Monitor GPU utilization and evict/scale nodes as needed.
- Rotate TLS certs 30 days before expiration.

Monitoring & alerting (recommended SLOs & thresholds)
- Availability SLO (control plane): 99.95% monthly
- Serving latency SLO (p50/p95/p99): baseline depends on model class; example p95 < 200ms for small models
- Alerts:
  - Control plane down: any control replica NotReady for >2 minutes -> P1
  - High error rate: 5xx rate >1% for 5m -> P2
  - Disk pressure on inference node -> P2

Incident playbook (summary)
1) Detect: alert fires (control plane or serving).
2) Triage: collect logs, metrics, and recent config changes.
3) Contain: scale down canary traffic, pause rollouts, or fail over to backup region.
4) Remediate: apply fix or rollback release.
5) Restore: verify system health and resume traffic.
6) Postmortem: within 72 hours, produce incident review and action items.

6) Customer Requirements Library (scoping checklist)
Network & security:
- CIDR ranges for VPC and desired subnets
- Firewall / Security Group rules to allow control <-> serving and metrics flows
- KMS/HSM type and key access policy
- Pen test and compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO27001 specifics)

Identity & access:
- Service account strategy (IRSA, IAM roles, or on-prem equivalent)
- RBAC roles and least privilege requirements

Operations & observability:
- Logging endpoint (ELK, Splunk, Cloud logs) and retention policy
- Prometheus/metrics retention and scrape targets
- SSO/SAML/OIDC provider for Redwood Console access

Maintenance windows & change management:
- Preferred maintenance window (TZ aware) and blackout periods
- Change approval process (who signs off on prod upgrades)

Legal & compliance artifacts to collect:
- Data classification for model inputs/outputs
- Audit log forwarding setup and retention proof
- Contractual uptime and incident response SLAs

7) Security, Secrets, and KMS Integration
- Do not store plaintext keys in Helm values files. Use sealed secrets or platform secret stores.
- Supported KMS providers: AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, HashiCorp Vault (HSM backing supported).
- Example: IAM role policy snippet (AWS) for decrypt permissions:
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [{
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:REGION:ACCOUNT:key/KEY_ID"
    }]
  }

8) Operational Playbooks and Runbooks (links & owners)
- Runbook: control-plane-unhealthy - owner: Platform SRE (oncall).
- Runbook: gpu-eviction - owner: Serving team.
- Runbook: offline-install - owner: Private Deployments.

Appendix A - Example values-serving.yaml (excerpt)
replicaCount: 3
image:
  repository: registry.internal/redwood/redwood-serving
  tag: 2029.11.1
resources:
  requests:
    cpu: "4000m"
    memory: "8Gi"
  limits:
    cpu: "8000m"
    memory: "16Gi"
nodeSelector:
  node.kubernetes.io/gpu: "true"
 tolerations:
  - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
    operator: "Exists"

Appendix B - Contact & ownership
- Private Deployments Product Lead: Priya Nair (pri.nair@redwood-inference.internal)
- Platform SRE oncall: redwood-platform@redwood-inference.internal
- Solutions Engineering: se-private-deploy@redwood-inference.internal

Appendix C - Change history
- 2029-11-15: Document created (Priya Nair).
- 2029-12-01: Added upgrade strategy and expanded day-2 ops checklist (reviewers: Ethan Morgan, Lena Ortiz).

If you are onboarding a customer, start with the Customer Requirements Library and then schedule a joint infra runbook session with the customer's network/security teams. For any deviations from the reference architectures above, contact the Private Deployments team before proceeding.
